docs.title: YAICLI: Your AI Assistant in Command Line
docs.text:
YAICLI is a powerful yet lightweight command-line AI assistant that brings the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-5.2 directly to your terminal. Interact with AI through multiple modes: have natural conversations, generate and execute shell commands, or get quick answers without leaving your workflow.

Supports both standard and deep reasoning models across all major LLM providers.

docs.title: ⚡ Agent Quick Start (3 steps)
docs.text:
1. Install and give it a key

pip install yaicli

# either export a key for the default OpenAI provider ...
export YAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
# ... or run a real command once (e.g. `ai "hi"`) and edit the config file
ai --version

2. Give the agent a real task

ai "Use your tools to find the 3 largest files in this repository and write a summary to REPORT.md"

The 12 built-in tools are loaded directly from the package, so the model can call them on the very first run — there is no --install-functions setup step.

3. Approve tool calls — allow once (y), for the session (a), permanently (A), or deny (n). See Permissions & Safety for the one safety rule explained properly.

docs.title: 🤖 Agent Loop with Built-in Tools
docs.text:
• Multi-step tasks: the model plans, calls tools, reads results and continues
  • 12 built-in tools: filesystem read/write/edit/search/info, image reading, shell execution, web fetch, web search and weather
  • MCP (optional): connect external MCP servers as additional tools

docs.title: 🛡️ Safe by Default
docs.text:
• Approval prompt for every tool call, with risk classes (read/write/network/exec)
  • Danger classification for shell commands and an audit log of every decision
  • Allow rules by tool name, shell argv prefix or file path glob
  • Guarded shell: timeout, process-group kill, filtered environment, workspace-confined cwd

docs.title: 📜 Headless & Scriptable
docs.text:
• -p/--print, -q/--quiet, --output-format json|stream-json
  • Clean stdout (result only) and stderr (logs/warnings), deterministic exit codes
  • --yes, --allowed-tools, --fail-on-tool-denied for non-interactive runs

docs.title: 🧠 Context Economy
docs.text:
• Tool-output truncation with full output spilled to disk
  • Token budget and turn-group-aligned trimming (no orphan tool messages)
  • Context-length self-heal and /compact

docs.title: 💻 Terminal Experience & Compatibility
docs.text:
• Real-time streaming, syntax highlighting, persistent chat sessions, file @ references, image input
  • 30+ providers and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — a compatibility layer, not the headline

docs.title: 🪶 Lightweight & scope
docs.text:
Metric (baseline = v0.18, macOS sandbox) Value ai --version startup (P50) ≈474–504 ms baseline → ≈40–45 ms measured with the v0.19 fast path (≈38 ms prototype) --help startup (P50) ≈519–568 ms (dominated by the CLI framework import) one-shot local overhead (ai "hi", no network) ≈1.5–1.6 s baseline, of which provider-SDK init is ≈0.9 s; further one-shot startup work is planned for v0.20 REPL ready (provider loaded) ≈1.55–1.75 s (provider SDK loads at startup; lazy initialization is planned for v0.20) base install closure 83 dists / 134.7 MB (includes optional fetch/search/MCP/cloud SDKs; dependency slimming is planned for v0.20) idle RSS ≈30 MB for --version; ≈65 MB for a REPL with the OpenAI SDK loaded background processes / daemons none

Measurement caveat: these numbers were measured on macOS inside a sandboxed benchmark environment, where file access is intercepted and absolute timings are inflated (expect 2–3× slower than a bare machine). Treat the relative deltas and proportions as the credible claim; absolute milliseconds will be re-measured on CI before they are used in release notes.

docs.title: 🔌 Compatibility
docs.text: YAICLI supports 30+ provider keys — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral and more — plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint via a custom BASE_URL. Provider support is a compatibility layer: the agent loop and tooling are the same for every provider. See the provider overview for the full matrix and per-provider setup.

docs.title: ⛰️  Features
docs.text:
• feat(cli): exit the REPL on a double Ctrl-C

Single Ctrl-C at the prompt still clears the current input line / cancels the current turn and keeps the session alive, but pressing Ctrl-C a second time within ~2 seconds now exits the REPL normally (like Ctrl-D); a completed prompt read resets the window, so a stray interrupt can never kill an interactive session. Generation interrupts follow the same counter: cancel the turn first, exit on the next Ctrl-C. One-shot SIGINT keeps exiting 130. Update the REPL help banner, README/docs (keyboard shortcuts, commands, SIGINT section) and the cli-and-rendering spec; add REPL tests for double-press exit, single-press survival and window reset. - (3c401ae) - Belingud - feat(permissions): risk-aware confirmation, rule-based allowlist and audit log

K06: tool risk classes (read/write/network/exec) and a shlex-based danger classifier gate execution: dangerous shell commands always need explicit confirmation (non-interactive => deny, even with TOOL_CONFIRM=false), --yes auto-allows only read risk, --allowed-tools grants globs for one run. tool_permissions.json v2 adds argv_prefix/path_glob rules while still reading the v1 always_allow format; writes are atomic and 0600. The confirmation prompt now shows the canonical arguments that will execute (shell command + danger reasons, fs_write target/mode, fs_edit diff head 40). Denied calls return structured {error: tool_denied, reason} results and tool_denied feeds --fail-on-tool-denied (exit 3). Every decision is appended to tool_audit.jsonl (best-effort, secret-redacted) and /permissions can list/revoke. - (c83c87c) - Belingud - feat(agent): context economy, retries and classified provider errors

K02: single truncation point for tool output (per-tool caps, head/tail marker, full text spilled to TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR), heuristic token estimator + model-window budget, turn-group-aligned history trimming that never orphans role=tool messages, context-length 400 self-heal (trim one group, retry once), bounded exponential retry for rate-limit/network/timeout/5xx before any content is streamed, depth-limit finish_reason/flag, /context usage summary and /compact. K05: all 39 provider registry keys now raise classified AgentError (kind/status/retryable) instead of returning API errors as assistant content or silently stopping; request-time and mid-stream failures are wrapped, empty/in-band error bodies raise, and TIMEOUT is forwarded consistently. - (3b8e27d) - Belingud - feat(cli): headless scripting contract and side-effect-free startup

K04: new -p/--print, --output-format text|json|stream-json, --json (shorthand), -q/--quiet, --max-turns, -y/--yes, --allowed-tools, --cwd and --fail-on-tool-denied flags; stdout carries only the result/events while warnings, errors and progress go to stderr; non-TTY runs skip prompt_toolkit/banner/Live; JSON object and NDJSON event contracts; exit codes 0/1/2/3/130/141; SIGINT semantics (one-shot 130, REPL clears/cancels); POSIX SIGPIPE restore so 'ai --help | head' no longer exits 1; --shell non-TTY only prints the command unless --yes. K21: new _faststart console entry answers --version from the static version without importing config/role/CLI (zero writes), python -m yaicli works, config/role/chat imports are write-free and lazy, ensure_config_file() creates config.ini 0600 under dir 0700 on first real run only, config dir resolution honours YAI_CONFIG_DIR/XDG/APPDATA and never writes /.config for an empty HOME. Includes the v0.19 error taxonomy/retry backbone (errors.py) and stderr console/EPIPE handling. - (978eec5) - Belingud - feat(functions): load built-in tools out of the box and harden shell execution

K01/K15: load the 12 packaged builtins directly, let same-named user copies override them, and warn about stale exported copies via functions_manifest.json (version+sha256). A broken function file is skipped with one warning instead of bricking every tool. --install-functions now exports editable copies; --reinstall-functions refreshes them. K03: shell tool gains timeout (default 120s, process-group kill), workspace-bounded cwd, env allowlist (TOOL_ENV_INHERIT opt-in), output cap and exits 124 on timeout; the old 3-substring danger blacklist is replaced by shlex/argv classification in tools/risk.py. - (77bd086) - Belingud

docs.title: 🐛 Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• fix(runtime): keep config imports write-free and make tests environment-safe

D7: key migrations for legacy config files are detected read-only at import and appended only by ensure_config_file() on a real run (deduped per CONFIG_PATH, skipped when the key already exists), so 'import yaicli.config' and '--help' no longer mutate an existing config.ini. T1: tests/conftest.py now sets the mock provider/credential environment before any yaicli module is imported, so the full suite is green in a fresh HOME/clean CI environment instead of failing five test_image tests with 'API_KEY is required'; the original environment is restored at session teardown. _faststart: flags after '--' are no longer treated as --version/-v (ai -- --version is a prompt). New regression tests for deferred migration, --help write-freedom and --/version parsing. - (bf39624) - Belingud - fix(agent): implement tool-output paging and harden shell env/spill handling

D6: fs_read_file gains optional offset/limit (characters, 0 = start/no limit) with per-file paging metadata (total_chars/returned_chars/truncated), so the truncation marker and docs that point the model at fs_read_file(offset/limit) for spilled tool output are truthful; legacy single-string/tuple inputs and the existing single/multi-file JSON shapes stay compatible. --cwd now wins over a stale exported YAI_WORKSPACE_ROOT: shell guardrail config is exported from cfg unconditionally (empty values skipped), matching entry._apply_cwd. Spill files for full tool outputs are created with 0600 permissions (best effort). Docs: context-limits paging table/semantics. Tests: schema contracts (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini), paging/edge cases, end-to-end tool-call paging, env precedence and spill mode. - (f19cac6) - Belingud - fix(permissions): block path-glob traversal and shell-syntax rule bypasses

D4: path_glob candidates are derived only from normalized paths (workspace-resolved with strict=False); the raw '..'-containing string is never a candidate and workspace-relative candidates that escape the workspace are rejected, so a rule like allowed/* can no longer be bypassed with allowed/../../victim.txt. Legitimate relative/absolute matches and the every-path-argument-must-match semantics are preserved. D5: argv_prefix rules only match a single simple command; the raw command is rejected when it contains shell control/expansion syntax (; | & < > backtick $( ${ <( >( CR/LF), so 'git status $(touch /tmp/x)' or piped/backtick variants require normal confirmation. 17 new regression tests (traversal/absolute/symlink escapes, parametrized control/substitution cases, legit plain args). - (4735f3d) - Belingud - fix(cli): keep machine-readable stdout clean in headless modes

D1/D2: re-point both the LLM client and its provider at the stderr console in machine-output mode, so provider verbose dumps ('Messages:', tools JSON) and API error bodies ('Error Response: {...}') can no longer corrupt --json/stream-json stdout; client/provider construction warnings are redirected to stderr as well. D3: compute headless intent in the CLI constructor (new defaulted print_mode/output_format/quiet kwargs) before the console, printer, client and prompt_toolkit session are created, so '-p --json' on a TTY never builds a PromptSession nor prints verbose config to stdout; entry.main passes the flags. D8: move the Gemini/MCP '@Function call'/'@MCP call' debug prints to stderr and drop ANSI escapes. Regression tests: polluting provider/client consoles under json/stream-json/--verbose, construction redirect, simulated-TTY constructor behaviour. - (5fd62bc) - Belingud

docs.title: ⛰️  Features
docs.text:
• feat!: confirm tool calls before execution

Add a confirmation gate before each tool/function call with four outcomes: allow once, allow for the session, allow permanently, or deny. Approvals are keyed by tool name (MCP prefix preserved); permanent approvals persist to ~/.config/yaicli/tool_permissions.json via an atomic write. Denied calls return a matched tool result so the provider request stays valid, and non-interactive sessions deny unapproved tools instead of blocking.

Also stream reasoning as append-only text rather than re-rendering it in the live region, fixing duplicated 'Thinking:' frames after large tool output.

BREAKING CHANGE: tool calls now require confirmation by default. Set TOOL_CONFIRM=false (env YAI_TOOL_CONFIRM=false) to restore silent execution. - (7cc64f0) - Belingud

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions to YAICLI are welcome! This page outlines how you can help improve the project.

docs.title: Ways to Contribute
docs.text:
There are several ways to contribute to YAICLI:

  • Bug Reports: Open an issue describing the bug and how to reproduce it
  • Feature Requests: Suggest new features or improvements
  • Code Contributions: Submit a pull request with your changes
  • Documentation: Help improve or translate the documentation

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or higher
  • uv, the Python project manager (https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)
  • Git
  • A GitHub account

docs.title: Setting Up Your Development Environment
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository on GitHub
  2. Clone your fork locally: 
    git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/yaicli.git
cd yaicli
  3. Create a virtual environment and activate it: 
    uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
  4. Install dependencies for development (dev tools, docs tooling and all provider extras): 
    uv sync --all-groups --all-extras

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
YAICLI follows these style guidelines:

  • Use Ruff for code formatting
  • Follow PEP 8 style guidelines
  • Write docstrings for all public functions, classes, and methods

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Before submitting a PR, make sure to run the tests and the linter:

uv run pytest
uv run ruff check yaicli tests

docs.title: Pull Request Process
docs.text:
1. Create a new branch for your feature or bugfix
  2. Make your changes
  3. Run the tests to ensure everything works
  4. Update the documentation if necessary
  5. Submit a pull request describing your changes

docs.title: Adding a New Provider
docs.text:
To add a new LLM provider to YAICLI:

  1. Create a new file in yaicli/llms/providers/ named after your provider (e.g., my_provider.py)
  2. Implement the provider class following the interface pattern of existing providers
  3. Register the provider in ProviderFactory.providers_map (yaicli/llms/provider.py); yaicli/llms/providers/__init__.py is empty. See Add a New Provider for the full walkthrough
  4. Update any configuration-related code to recognize the new provider
  5. Add tests for your provider in the tests/llms/ directory

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
When contributing documentation:

  1. Follow the existing structure
  2. Use Markdown for all documentation files
  3. Test changes locally using MkDocs (docs tooling is in the docs dependency group): 
    uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: This page addresses common questions and issues encountered when using YAICLI.

docs.title: What is YAICLI?
docs.text: YAICLI is a lightweight agent that runs in your terminal. Given a task, it can plan, call its built-in tools (read/write files, search the web, run shell commands), read the results and continue until the task is done. It also works as a classic chat/quick-answer CLI and supports 30+ LLM providers.

docs.title: What LLM providers are supported?
docs.text: YAICLI supports multiple providers including: - OpenAI (GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, etc.) - Google Gemini - Claude (Anthropic) - Cohere - Mistral - Ollama - Many others (see Providers Overview)

docs.title: Is an internet connection required?
docs.text: Yes, for most providers. YAICLI communicates with LLM APIs that require internet access. However, you can use local models with providers like Ollama.

docs.title: How is my data handled?
docs.text: YAICLI stores your conversation history locally. Your prompts and API responses are sent to the LLM provider you configure, according to their privacy policies. No data is sent to YAICLI developers.

docs.title: Why am I getting "command not found" after installing?
docs.text:
Make sure your Python scripts directory is in your PATH. Try these solutions:

# Option 1: Find the installation location
which ai

# Option 2: Add to PATH (add to .bashrc or .zshrc)
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

docs.title: How do I set up my API key?
docs.text:
You can set your API key in two ways: 1. In the config file (config.ini inside the config directory — ~/.config/yaicli by default, or $YAI_CONFIG_DIR / $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yaicli when set) 2. As an environment variable (export YAI_API_KEY="your-key") — preferred for scripts and shared machines

YAICLI does not load .env files; use one of the options above (a .env file has no effect).

docs.title: Can I use multiple API keys for different providers?
docs.text:
Yes! You can create separate configuration sections or switch providers using environment variables:

# Use OpenAI
export YAI_PROVIDER=openai
export YAI_API_KEY=sk-...

# Use Gemini (in another session or after changing vars)
export YAI_PROVIDER=gemini
export YAI_API_KEY=AI...

docs.title: How do I save a chat session?
docs.text:
In chat mode, use the /save command followed by a title: 

💬 > /save "Python Tips"

Or start a named session that will be automatically saved: 

ai --chat "Python Tips"

docs.title: How do I control output formatting?
docs.text:
Use the --justify option to control text alignment: 

ai --justify center "Write a poem about AI"

Options include: default, left, center, right, and full.

For scripts, use --output-format json (single JSON object), --output-format stream-json (NDJSON events) or -q/--quiet (answer only). See Headless & Scripting.

docs.title: How do I disable streaming responses?
docs.text:
Use the --no-stream flag or set STREAM=false in your config: 

ai --no-stream "What is the capital of France?"

docs.title: How do I change the code highlighting theme?
docs.text:
Set the CODE_THEME in your config file: 

CODE_THEME = monokai

Use any other Pygments theme name here (comments must be on their own line).

docs.title: How do I execute shell commands safely?
docs.text:
Use shell mode with the -s or --shell flag: 

ai -s "Find all PNG files in the current directory"
You'll be prompted to review and optionally edit commands before execution.

When the model runs execute_shell_command as a tool, the approval prompt, danger classification, timeout and filtered environment apply automatically; see Permissions & Safety.

docs.title: Why am I getting API errors?
docs.text:
Common causes: - Invalid API key - Rate limits or quota exceeded - Network connectivity issues - Incompatible model for your provider

Usually you will see a error message in output like 429 too many requests.

Try running with the verbose flag to see detailed error information: 

ai --verbose "Test query"

docs.title: How do I fix "SSL Certificate Verification Failed"?
docs.text:
This typically happens in corporate environments with SSL inspection. Try:

# Not recommended for security reasons, but may be necessary
export PYTHONWARNINGS="ignore:Unverified HTTPS request"
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/corporate/certificate.pem

docs.title: How do I update YAICLI?
docs.text:
# Using pip
pip install --upgrade yaicli

# Using pipx
pipx upgrade yaicli

# Using uv
uv tool upgrade yaicli

The built-in tools load directly from the installed package in v0.19+, so a normal upgrade needs no extra step. If you previously exported function files with ai --install-functions, refresh them with ai --reinstall-functions (custom files are kept). See Upgrade Notes for behaviour changes and new config keys.

docs.title: Why are my non-ASCII characters displaying incorrectly?
docs.text:
Make sure your terminal supports UTF-8 and has a compatible font. On Windows, you might need to: 

chcp 65001  # Set console code page to UTF-8

docs.title: How do I create custom roles?
docs.text:
Create a new role: 

ai --create-role "SQL Expert"

Then use it: 

ai --role "SQL Expert" "Optimize this query"

docs.title: Can I use function calling?
docs.text:
Function calling is enabled by default and the 12 built-in tools load directly from the package — there is no setup step: 

ai "check the weather in New York"
ai --list-functions   # show the loaded tools (builtin/user)

If you need editable copies of the built-in definitions, export them with ai --install-functions; a copy overrides the built-in with the same tool name. Every tool call is confirmed by default; see Permissions & Safety.

docs.title: How do I create custom functions?
docs.text:
Add your function definitions to ~/.config/yaicli/functions/; each file must define a Function(OpenAISchema) class with a classmethod execute. Restart ai afterwards.

If you recently upgraded YAICLI and keep exported copies of the built-in definitions, run ai --reinstall-functions so those copies match the new version (custom files are preserved).

See Advanced Usage — Function Calling for the complete custom-function guide.

docs.title: How do I use MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
docs.text:
Enable MCP with: 

ai --enable-mcp "Search for the latest AI research papers"

Configure MCP in: 

~/.config/yaicli/mcp.json

docs.title: How can I contribute to YAICLI?
docs.text: We welcome contributions! See the contributing guidelines for details on: - Reporting bugs - Suggesting features - Submitting pull requests - Code standards

docs.title: Where can I report bugs or request features?
docs.text: Please submit issues on the GitHub repository.

docs.title: Getting Started with YAICLI
docs.text: YAICLI is a lightweight agent that runs in your terminal. It can read and edit files, search the web and run shell commands through its built-in tools, and it keeps working through a task until it is done. This page gets you from zero to a completed multi-step task in three steps.

docs.title: Step 1 — Install and give it a key
docs.text:
pip install yaicli

# Option A: keep the key in an environment variable (recommended for scripts/CI)
export YAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

# Option B: run a real command once (e.g. `ai "hi"`); it creates the config file, then edit it
ai "hi"
nano ~/.config/yaicli/config.ini

pipx install yaicli and uv tool install yaicli work the same way. Verify the install with ai --version (this fast path does not read or write any config).

docs.title: Step 2 — Give the agent a real task
docs.text:
ai "Use your tools to find the 3 largest files in this repository and write a summary to REPORT.md"

The model chooses the tools it needs from the built-in set and reads each result before deciding the next step:

Tool group Built-in tools Filesystem (read) fs_get_filesystem_info, fs_list_directory, fs_read_file, fs_read_image, fs_search_files Filesystem (write) fs_write_file, fs_edit_file, fs_file_operations Shell (exec) execute_shell_command Network fetch_webpage, web_search, get_weather

You do not need to run ai --install-functions first: the definitions ship with the package and are loaded directly. ai --list-functions shows all 12 built-in tools on a fresh install.

docs.title: Step 3 — Approve tool calls (the one safety rule to learn)
docs.text:
Before a tool runs, YAICLI asks:

╭─ Confirm tool call ─────────────────────────────────────╮
│ execute_shell_command({"shell_command": "du -sh ."})    │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
Execute tool? [y]once, [a]session, [A]always, [n]o:
Key Meaning y Allow this call only a Allow this tool for the rest of the session A Always allow — saved to tool_permissions.json n Deny — the model receives the refusal and adapts

Read-level tools are marked read; write, network and shell tools are classified more strictly, and a dangerous shell command (such as rm -r -f, mkfs, dd of=/dev/* or curl … | sh) always requires an explicit confirmation. In scripts, allow tools up front with --allowed-tools.

That's the whole safety model — the details (rules, audit log, headless approval) are in Permissions & Safety.

docs.title: Everyday Usage
docs.text:
Once the agent works, the classic modes are still there:

# Quick answer (no tool loop needed)
ai "What is the capital of France?"

# Interactive chat session
ai --chat

# Generate and execute a shell command
ai --shell "Create a backup of my Documents folder"

# Generate code (Python by default)
ai --code "Write a function to sort a list"

# Pipe input
cat error.log | ai "Explain these errors"

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Run ai --template to see the full default configuration (the file itself is created on the first real model run). The config directory is resolved in this order: YAI_CONFIG_DIR → XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yaicli → %APPDATA%/yaicli (Windows) → ~/.config/yaicli. The file is created with mode 0600 because it may store API keys; environment variables are the preferred way to provide keys.

YAICLI uses a layered configuration approach:

  • Command-line arguments (highest priority)
  • Environment variables
  • Config file (config.ini)
  • Sensible defaults (lowest priority)

See Configuration for every option.

docs.title: Check the agent is ready
docs.text:
ai --list-functions     # should list 12 builtin tools
ai --list-providers     # should list the provider keys
ai --version            # fast, no config writes

If --list-functions lists nothing, the built-in function loader failed for every file; reinstall the package (pip install -U yaicli) and open an issue with the warning printed at startup.

docs.title: Script It
docs.text:
The same agent runs headless — stdout carries only the result, everything else goes to stderr:

ai -p "summarize the changes in the last 5 commits" --output-format json | jq .content

# Answer-only output, safe for pipelines
ai -q -p "count the TODO comments in src/" > todos.txt

# Non-interactive tool approval for a CI job
ai -p "run the test suite and summarize failures" --allowed-tools "execute_shell_command" -y

See Headless & Scripting for the JSON schema, exit codes and signal handling.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: YAICLI can be installed using several methods. Choose the one that best suits your needs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • Python 3.10 or higher

docs.title: Using pip (Recommended)
docs.text:
The simplest way to install YAICLI is using pip:

pip install yaicli

docs.title: Using pipx (Isolated Environment)
docs.text:
If you prefer to install the tool in an isolated environment:

pipx install yaicli

docs.title: Using uv (Faster Installation)
docs.text:
For faster installation with the uv package manager:

uv tool install yaicli

docs.title: Installing with Optional Dependencies
docs.text: YAICLI offers several optional dependency groups that you can install based on your needs:

docs.title: All Dependencies
docs.text:
# Using pip
pip install 'yaicli[all]'

# Using uv
uv tool install 'yaicli[all]'

docs.title: Specific Provider Support
docs.text:
# Using pip
pip install 'yaicli[ollama,cohere,doubao,huggingface,gemini,mistral]'

# Using uv
uv tool install 'yaicli[ollama,cohere,doubao,huggingface,gemini,mistral]'

docs.title: Installing from Source
docs.text:
For the latest development version:

git clone https://github.com/belingud/yaicli.git
cd yaicli
pip install .

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text:
To verify that YAICLI was installed correctly:

ai --version            # fast path: prints the version, no config writes
ai --help               # full command reference
ai --list-functions     # should list 12 builtin tools (they work out of the box)
ai --list-providers     # should list the provider keys

python -m yaicli --version works as well if the ai script is not on your PATH.

docs.title: First-Time Setup
docs.text:
After installation, run a real command once (for example ai "hi"); the default configuration file is created on first use:

ai "hi"

Then edit the configuration file to add your API key and customize settings. The config directory is resolved in this order: YAI_CONFIG_DIR → XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yaicli → %APPDATA%/yaicli (Windows) → ~/.config/yaicli. The file is created with mode 0600 because it may contain an API key; alternatively export the key and skip editing the file (plain ai with no prompt only prints help and does not create state):

export YAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

# Open the config with your preferred editor (default path on Linux/macOS)
nano ~/.config/yaicli/config.ini

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Upgrade the package the same way you installed it:

pip install -U yaicli        # pip
pipx upgrade yaicli          # pipx
uv tool upgrade yaicli       # uv

docs.title: Do I need --reinstall-functions?
docs.text:
Not for a normal upgrade. Since v0.19 the built-in tool definitions load directly from the installed package, so new versions take effect immediately.

You only need to refresh function files if you previously exported copies into the functions directory (ai --install-functions) or edited a built-in tool:

ai --reinstall-functions    # refresh exported built-in copies (custom files are kept)
ai --list-functions         # verify sources and stale-copy warnings

A user function file with the same tool name as a built-in wins over the built-in. If a stale copy is detected, YAICLI prints a one-line warning but keeps working.

See Upgrade Notes for the complete v0.19 change list (new config keys, environment filtering for shell tools, output truncation, permissions v2, headless flags, state paths) and rollback instructions.

docs.text:
ai --verbose "hello"

Verbose mode prints the effective configuration, the current role, the provider request messages/tools, and tracebacks for handled errors. Only API_KEY is masked — be careful when sharing the output because provider-specific credentials may appear.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Successful runs exit 0; handled failures exit 1 (configuration errors, provider/API errors, retry exhaustion, missing credentials, no input, depth limit). Usage errors exit 2, a denied tool with --fail-on-tool-denied exits 3, SIGINT exits 130 and a broken pipe exits 0/141. See Exit Codes and Headless & Scripting. In --chat mode, a failed turn prints the error and keeps the session alive instead of exiting.

docs.title: Isolate the environment
docs.text:
# fresh config/roles/functions in a temp HOME
HOME=/tmp/yaicli-debug ai --verbose "hello"

# inspect the default config template
ai --template

# print the effective config file path (shown by --verbose)

Common causes:

  • Provider errors: verify PROVIDER with ai --list-providers, then check MODEL, BASE_URL and the API key.
  • Function changes not taking effect: built-in definitions load directly from the installed package; only exported copies in ~/.config/yaicli/functions/ can be stale. Run ai --list-functions (it reports sources and stale copies), then ai --reinstall-functions to refresh exported built-in copies.
  • Network/proxy: HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY are honoured by the HTTP stack; an invalid BASE_URL causes connection errors.
  • MCP: ~/.config/yaicli/mcp.json must be valid JSON; run ai --list-mcp.

When reporting a bug, include the command, the expected vs actual behaviour, the exit code, and the relevant (redacted) verbose output.

docs.title: Conversation & History Management
docs.text: YAICLI provides robust conversation history management features to help you maintain context and revisit past interactions. This page explains how the history system works and how to manage your chat history.

docs.title: Command History
docs.text: YAICLI maintains a history of your commands and interactions, allowing you to: - Search through previous commands - Reuse past queries - Keep track of your AI conversations

docs.title: History Storage
docs.text:
By default, command history is stored in $XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history when XDG_STATE_HOME is set, otherwise in ~/.yaicli_history (%USERPROFILE%\.yaicli_history on Windows).

The history file uses a simple text format with each command on a new line.

docs.title: History Size
docs.text:
You can configure the maximum number of history entries to retain:

[core]
MAX_HISTORY=500

Or using an environment variable:

export YAI_MAX_HISTORY=1000

docs.title: Viewing History
docs.text:
In interactive mode, use the /his command to view your chat history:

💬 > /his
Chat History:
1 User: What is quantum computing?
    Assistant: Quantum computing is a type of computation...
2 User: What are qubits?
    Assistant: Qubits (quantum bits) are the basic...

docs.title: Searching History
docs.text:
Use Ctrl+R to search through your command history:

  1. Press Ctrl+R
  2. Type part of a previous command
  3. Press Ctrl+R again to cycle through matching results
  4. Press Enter to select the current match

docs.title: Auto-Suggestion
docs.text:
YAICLI can suggest commands based on your history as you type. Enable this feature in your config:

[core]
AUTO_SUGGEST=true

When enabled, YAICLI will show suggestions in light gray text as you type. Press the right arrow key to accept a suggestion.

docs.title: Chat Persistence
docs.text:
Chat sessions can be persistent or temporary:

  • Persistent Session: Automatically saved with a title
  • Temporary Session: Not saved unless explicitly requested

To start a persistent chat session:

ai --chat "Python programming"

To convert a temporary session to persistent:

💬 > /save "Python programming"
Chat saved as: Python programming

docs.title: Chat Storage Location
docs.text:
Chat history is stored in: - Default: A temporary directory specific to your system - Configurable through CHAT_HISTORY_DIR setting

[core]
CHAT_HISTORY_DIR=/path/to/custom/directory
MAX_SAVED_CHATS=20

docs.title: Listing Saved Chats
docs.text:
To list your saved chat sessions:

# From command line
ai --list-chats

# From interactive mode
💬 > /list

This displays a numbered list of saved chats with their creation dates.

docs.title: Loading Saved Chats
docs.text:
You can load saved chats in two ways:

# From command line (using the chat title)
ai --chat "Python programming"

# From interactive mode (using the chat index from /list)
💬 > /load 3

docs.title: Deleting Saved Chats
docs.text:
To delete a saved chat:

# From interactive mode
💬 > /del 3

This will permanently remove the selected chat session.

docs.title: Context Window
docs.text: YAICLI automatically manages the conversation context based on: - The model's context window limitations - The number of messages in the current session - The complexity and length of each message

docs.title: Clearing Context
docs.text:
To clear the current conversation context:

💬 > /clear

This removes all previous messages from the current session's context but does not delete saved chat history.

docs.title: Chat File Format
docs.text:
Chat sessions are stored as JSON files in CHAT_HISTORY_DIR (see Configuration). The current format keeps every field of a message, so restoring a session preserves tool calls, images, and reasoning content:

{
  "title": "Chat Title",
  "date": "2024-06-01T12:00:00+00:00",
  "history": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "look at before.png"
    },
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "",
      "reasoning": "I should read the image first.",
      "tool_calls": [
        {
          "id": "call_1",
          "name": "fs_read_image",
          "arguments": "{\"image_paths\": [\"before.png\"]}"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "role": "tool",
      "content": "{\"images\": [...]}",
      "name": "fs_read_image",
      "tool_call_id": "call_1"
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "and this one?",
      "images": [
        {
          "data": "<base64 or URL>",
          "media_type": "image/png",
          "is_url": false
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Optional fields are written only when they are set: name, tool_call_id, tool_calls, reasoning, and images. A tool_calls entry is {"id", "name", "arguments"}; an images entry is {"data", "media_type", "is_url"}.

docs.title: Atomic Saves
docs.text:
Sessions are written atomically: the new JSON is written to a hidden temporary file in the same directory (.filename.pid.tmp), flushed/fsync-ed, and then moved over the target file with os.replace. Consequences:

  • an interrupted or failed save never truncates or corrupts the previously saved session;
  • FileChatManager writes the replacement file before deleting older sessions with the same title, so a failed /save keeps the previous version loadable;
  • a failed save still raises ChatSaveError and is reported in the CLI.

docs.title: Compatibility and Migration
docs.text:
Old session files that only contain {"role", "content"} messages still load: missing optional fields default to empty. New files are a superset of the legacy format, so no explicit migration step is required — loading then saving a session rewrites it in the current format. The same applies to tool_calls/images/reasoning: sessions saved by older versions simply do not contain them.

You can still edit a session file manually. Keep the top-level title/date/history keys; each message must at least have role and content, and any tool_calls/images entries must keep the shapes shown above (a damaged entry is skipped, but tool results whose assistant tool_calls were removed will make provider requests invalid).

If a session file is corrupted, fix or delete that JSON file; the other sessions are unaffected.

docs.title: Disabling History
docs.text:
You can disable command history saving completely by setting:

[core]
MAX_HISTORY=0

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Regular Cleaning: Periodically review and delete unnecessary chat sessions
  2. Meaningful Titles: Use descriptive titles for your persistent chats
  3. Context Awareness: Clear context when switching topics within the same session
  4. Backup: Occasionally backup your chat history directory for important conversations

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Explore debugging and logging
  • Check out prompt templates

docs.title: Prompt Template System
docs.text: YAICLI features a powerful and flexible prompt template system that allows you to define custom roles and behaviors for your AI assistant. This page explains how to use and customize the prompt system.

docs.title: Understanding Roles
docs.text: In YAICLI, a "role" is a predefined set of instructions, preferences, and behaviors assigned to the AI. Roles help guide how the AI responds to your queries.

docs.title: Default Roles
docs.text: YAICLI ships with three built-in roles: DEFAULT (general-purpose assistant), Shell Command Generator (used by --shell/execute mode), and Code Assistant (used by --code). Built-in role files are seeded into ~/.config/yaicli/roles/ on first run and can be overridden (a warning is shown unless ROLE_MODIFY_WARNING=false).

docs.title: Creating Custom Roles
docs.text:
You can create custom roles to tailor the AI's behavior for specific tasks or domains:

# Create a new role through interactive prompting
ai --create-role "SQL Expert"

# You'll be asked to provide a description for this role

When creating a role, you'll be prompted to describe how the AI should behave in that role. For example:

Please provide a description for the SQL Expert role:

You are an expert SQL database engineer with deep knowledge of database 
optimization, query design, and best practices across multiple SQL dialects 
including MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, and Microsoft SQL Server. 

When asked about SQL, you should:
1. Consider the specific dialect if mentioned, or clarify which dialect you're using
2. Provide optimized queries with explanations of your optimization choices
3. Consider indexing, query planning, and performance implications
4. Format SQL with proper indentation and capitalization of keywords

docs.title: Using Custom Roles
docs.text:
Once created, you can use your custom roles:

# Use in direct query mode
ai --role "SQL Expert" "Optimize this query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true"

# Use in chat mode
ai --chat --role "SQL Expert"

Role selection applies to direct queries, --chat, and --code. --shell always uses the built-in Shell Command Generator role (a non-default --role is ignored with a warning).

docs.title: Managing Roles
docs.text:
YAICLI provides commands to manage your roles:

# List all available roles
ai --list-roles

# View a specific role's description
ai --show-role "SQL Expert"

# Delete a role
ai --delete-role "SQL Expert"

docs.title: Role Storage
docs.text:
Custom roles are stored in: - Linux/macOS: ~/.config/yaicli/roles/ - Windows: C:\Users\<username>\.config\yaicli\roles\

Each role is saved as a JSON file with the role name.

docs.title: Setting a Default Role
docs.text:
You can set a default role in your configuration file:

[core]
DEFAULT_ROLE=SQL Expert

Or using an environment variable:

export YAI_DEFAULT_ROLE="SQL Expert"

docs.title: Role Structure
docs.text:
Roles are defined as JSON files with the following structure:

{
  "name": "Role Name",
  "prompt": "You are a helpful assistant. Reply concisely.",
  "variables": {
    "_os": "macOS",
    "_shell": "zsh"
  }
}

name and prompt are required (the prompt must be a non-empty string and is the "description" requested by ai --create-role). variables is optional: if omitted, YAICLI fills _os and _shell from auto-detection. The prompt is passed through Python str.format(), so literal braces must be doubled ({{ and }}), and unknown {name} placeholders cause the role to be rejected with a load error.

docs.title: Creating Roles Manually
docs.text:
You can create roles manually by adding JSON files to the roles directory:

  1. Create a file in ~/.config/yaicli/roles/ (for example my_role.json)
  2. Add the role structure shown above; the name field is what --role uses, regardless of the file name
  3. Restart YAICLI or run ai --list-roles to see your new role

docs.title: Role Modification Warning
docs.text:
By default, YAICLI will warn you when attempting to modify built-in roles. To disable this warning:

[core]
ROLE_MODIFY_WARNING=false

docs.title: Best Practices for Writing Role Descriptions
docs.text:
For the most effective custom roles:

  1. Be Specific: Clearly define the expertise and focus area
  2. Set Boundaries: Specify what the AI should and should not address
  3. Format Guidelines: Include preferred output formats, styles, or conventions
  4. Examples: When helpful, include examples of desired responses
  5. Context: Add relevant domain knowledge or context that might help the AI

docs.title: Technical Writer
docs.text:
You are a technical writer specializing in creating clear, concise documentation.

When responding:
1. Use plain language and avoid jargon unless necessary
2. Structure content with logical headings and lists
3. Focus on practical examples and use cases
4. Include both beginner and advanced perspectives
5. Use consistent terminology throughout

For code examples, include comments explaining key concepts.

docs.title: Data Analyst
docs.text:
You are a data analyst with expertise in statistics, data visualization, and data manipulation.

When analyzing data or answering queries:
1. Consider statistical validity and assumptions
2. Suggest appropriate visualization techniques
3. Recommend efficient data processing approaches
4. Highlight potential biases or limitations
5. Provide code examples in Python using pandas, matplotlib, or similar libraries

Always emphasize data integrity and ethical considerations in your analysis.

docs.title: System Administrator
docs.text:
You are a system administrator experienced with Linux, Windows, and cloud environments.

When providing assistance:
1. Prioritize security best practices
2. Consider compatibility across different systems
3. Provide step-by-step instructions with explanations
4. Suggest monitoring and maintenance practices
5. Mention potential pitfalls or issues to watch for

For shell commands, explain what each command does and any flags or options used.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Learn about chat history management
  • Explore function calling capabilities
  • Check out debugging and logs

docs.title: Upgrade Notes
docs.text: This page explains what changes when you upgrade to v0.19 and what (if anything) you must do. Old config files keep working: newly added keys simply fall back to their defaults.

docs.title: Upgrade the package
docs.text:
# pip
pip install -U yaicli

# pipx
pipx upgrade yaicli

# uv
uv tool upgrade yaicli

Then verify:

ai --version
ai --list-functions     # 12 builtin tools should be listed
ai --list-providers

docs.title: Do I need to reinstall functions?
docs.text:
Usually no. Since v0.19 the 12 built-in tool definitions load directly from the installed package, so a fresh install (and a fresh HOME) can call tools on the first run. ai --install-functions is no longer part of the setup.

You only need to refresh function files if you have exported copies in the functions directory (<config-dir>/functions/, normally ~/.config/yaicli/functions/), for example because you ran ai --install-functions before, or you edited a built-in tool:

ai --reinstall-functions    # overwrite stale built-in copies (custom names are kept)
ai --list-functions         # shows builtin/user source and warns about stale copies

If a user file has the same tool name as a built-in, the user file wins. If you want the new built-in version, delete the old copy (or run --reinstall-functions) and restart ai. YAICLI only warns about stale copies; it never silently overwrites your customisations.

docs.title: What changed in v0.19
docs.text: Area Change Action needed Built-in tools Loaded directly from the package (12 tools out of the box); --install-functions = export editable copies; --list-functions shows builtin/user source None, unless you keep exported copies — then run --reinstall-functions Shell tool environment Commands receive a filtered environment by default (YAI_API_KEY and other secrets are not passed) Set TOOL_ENV_INHERIT=true to restore the old full-environment behaviour Shell tool timeout TOOL_TIMEOUT (default 120 s); timed-out commands are killed with their whole process group (exit code 124 in the tool result) Check long-running commands; raise TOOL_TIMEOUT if needed Shell danger checks Replaced the old 3-substring blacklist with argv/flag analysis: dangerous commands need an extra confirmation, and git add is no longer blocked None Tool output size Results are truncated (TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS, default 32000 chars); the full output is spilled to TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR Raise the cap or set 0 to disable; the model can page spilled files back with fs_read_file Context window Token budget (CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS), turn-group trimming and context-length self-heal; /context and /compact added None; tune the budget for small-window models Permissions Risk classes, tool_permissions.json v2 rules (argv_prefix, path_glob), audit log (TOOL_AUDIT), /permissions command Old always_allow string list stays valid; add rules for finer control Headless New flags -p/--print, --output-format, -q/--quiet, --max-turns, -y/--yes, --allowed-tools, --cwd, --fail-on-tool-denied; clean stdout/stderr split; exit codes 0/1/2/3/130/141 Update scripts that parsed decorated output; see Headless & Scripting One-shot exit codes Handled errors now exit non-zero in one-shot mode (previously 0); depth-limit exhaustion exits non-zero (EXIT_ON_DEPTH_LIMIT) Add error handling to scripts that relied on exit 0 Interrupts One-shot SIGINT exits 130; REPL prompt Ctrl+C clears the line (press twice quickly to exit); Ctrl+D exits None Startup --version fast path: no config/role imports, zero filesystem writes, much faster; --help/--template no longer create state files None Config & state paths YAI_CONFIG_DIR / XDG_CONFIG_HOME (and %APPDATA% on Windows) are honoured; config dir 0700 / config.ini 0600; new files are created on demand Move config if you want XDG locations; existing ~/.config/yaicli keeps working History file Uses XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history when XDG_STATE_HOME is set, otherwise ~/.yaicli_history None python -m python -m yaicli --version now works None

docs.title: New configuration keys
docs.text:
Add these to config.ini only if you want non-default values (see Configuration); ai --template prints the full template.

Key Default Purpose TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS 32000 Per-tool-result character cap (0 = unlimited) TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR <chat history>/tool-outputs Where full tool outputs are stored CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS 0 (70% of model window) Per-request token budget TOOL_TIMEOUT 120 Shell command timeout in seconds TOOL_ENV_INHERIT false Pass the full parent environment to shell tools WORKSPACE_ROOT empty (current dir) Directory shell tools are confined to RETRY_ENABLED true Retry retryable API failures RETRY_MAX 2 Maximum retry attempts RETRY_BASE_DELAY 1.0 Base backoff delay (seconds) EXIT_ON_DEPTH_LIMIT true One-shot exits non-zero when the tool-round limit is reached TOOL_AUDIT true Append tool decisions to tool_audit.jsonl

docs.title: Where state lives now
docs.text:
The config directory is resolved in this order:

  1. YAI_CONFIG_DIR (explicit override)
  2. XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yaicli
  3. %APPDATA%/yaicli on Windows
  4. ~/.config/yaicli

Files in the config directory:

File / directory Purpose config.ini Main configuration (created 0600; may contain an API key) roles/ Role definitions functions/ User/exported tool definitions (override built-ins by tool name) functions_manifest.json Package version + hashes used to detect stale exported copies mcp.json MCP server configuration tool_permissions.json Persistent tool allow rules (v2) tool_audit.jsonl Tool decision audit log tool-outputs/ Spilled full tool outputs (by default under the chat history dir)

HISTORY_FILE is separate: $XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history when XDG_STATE_HOME is set, otherwise ~/.yaicli_history. Chat sessions live under CHAT_HISTORY_DIR.

docs.title: If something behaves unexpectedly
docs.text:
1. Run ai --list-functions — stale exported copies are flagged there. Refresh with ai --reinstall-functions.
  2. Run ai --verbose "..." and check the effective config file path and provider/model.
  3. Reproduce with a clean config dir: YAI_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) ai "hi".
  4. Check the new defaults: environment filtering (TOOL_ENV_INHERIT), output truncation (TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS), and shell timeout (TOOL_TIMEOUT) are the most likely reasons an old workflow behaves differently.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
To go back to the previous release:

pip install 'yaicli==0.18.0'

Your config.ini and permissions file remain readable by the old version (unknown keys are ignored); tool_permissions.json stays backward compatible because v2 only adds keys. Remove tool_audit.jsonl / tool-outputs/ if you no longer need them.

docs.title: Add a New Provider
docs.text: This tutorial walks through adding an LLM provider. Read .trellis/spec/py/provider-guidelines.md first; it is the authoritative coding guide for the provider layer.

docs.title: 1. Pick the narrowest base class
docs.text:
Provider classes live in yaicli/llms/providers/. Most providers only need a base URL, a client class, and a parameter mapping:

Base Use when Examples OpenAIProvider (openai_provider.py) OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API XAI, Together, SiliconFlow, Chutes, ModelScope, Moonshot, OpenRouter, Targon, Yi OpenAIProvider + custom CLIENT_CLS OpenAI wire format, different SDK client Doubao (Ark), Cerebras, Fireworks OpenAICompatibleProvider Generic /chat/completions endpoints with proxy quirks openai-compatible AnthropicProvider (anthropic_provider.py) Anthropic Messages API family Anthropic Bedrock/Vertex, LongCat (Anthropic format) GeminiProvider (gemini_provider.py) Google GenAI SDK (native Gemini protocol) Gemini, VertexAI Provider directly Native SDK with its own protocol Ollama, Cohere, Mistral

The two abstract methods are completion() (a generator of LLMResponse) and detect_tool_role(). _convert_messages() has a default OpenAI-format implementation; override it only when the wire format differs.

docs.title: 2. Create the provider module
docs.text:
Create yaicli/llms/providers/<name>_provider.py:

from .openai_provider import OpenAIProvider


class MyProvider(OpenAIProvider):
    """My LLM provider, OpenAI-compatible."""

    DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://api.example.com/v1"
    COMPLETION_PARAMS_KEYS = {
        "model": "MODEL",
        "temperature": "TEMPERATURE",
        "top_p": "TOP_P",
        "max_tokens": "MAX_TOKENS",
        "timeout": "TIMEOUT",
        "extra_body": "EXTRA_BODY",
    }

Provider-specific config keys (AK/SK, HF_PROVIDER, AWS_REGION, ...) are read with config.get(); they are not in DEFAULT_CONFIG_MAP, so they have no YAI_* environment alias unless you add them there. Use DEFAULT_BASE_URL for the endpoint, keep the API key in config["API_KEY"], and never instantiate the SDK client at import time.

docs.title: 3. Register the provider key
docs.text:
Add the provider to ProviderFactory.providers_map in yaicli/llms/provider.py (the yaicli/llms/providers/__init__.py file is empty):

providers_map = {
    ...
    "my-provider": (".providers.my_provider", "MyProvider"),
}

The key is the exact PROVIDER= value users set; only lowercasing is applied. Registry key and class name are independent ("openai-azure" → OpenAIAzure). The factory imports modules lazily, so a missing optional SDK only fails when that provider is selected.

docs.title: 4. Optional dependency (if the SDK is not core)
docs.text: If the provider SDK is optional, add an extra for it in pyproject.toml ([project.optional-dependencies]) and include it in the all extra. Import the SDK at the top of your provider module (it is only imported when selected) — never add it to the shared yaicli import path.

docs.title: 5. Images and special capabilities
docs.text: If the API cannot accept images, add the provider key to NO_VISION_PROVIDERS in yaicli/const.py; CLI._build_messages() then warns and strips images for that provider.

docs.title: 6. Tests
docs.text:
• Add tests/llms/test_<name>_provider.py. Mock the SDK client (never call a real API) and follow the fixture/mocking style of tests/llms/test_deepseek_provider.py; patch schema helpers on the provider module, not on yaicli.tools.
  • Add the new key to expected_providers in tests/llms/test_provider.py::TestProviderFactory::test_known_provider_types; it asserts the exact registry key set and fails until updated.

docs.title: 7. Documentation
docs.text:
• Add docs/providers/<name>.md.
  • Add a row/link to docs/providers/overview.md.
  • Add the page to nav: in mkdocs.yml and the provider list in README.md.

docs.title: 8. Verify
docs.text:
uv run pytest tests/llms -q
ruff check yaicli tests
# black-box check that the key is registered and can be instantiated:
PYTHONPATH=. python -m yaicli.entry --list-providers
# with an isolated config/HOME, exercise the provider name:
HOME=/tmp/yaicli-dev uv run python -m yaicli.entry --version

ai --list-providers reads the registry, so a key missing there is a registration bug, not a documentation bug.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: This page describes how YAICLI is put together and where to start when changing it. User-facing behaviour is documented under docs/usage/; coding conventions live in CLAUDE.md and .trellis/spec/.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
_faststart.py (thin console entry; -v/--version fast path, EPIPE-safe)
  └─ entry.py (Typer CLI; headless flags -> CLI.configure_headless, exit-code mapping)
       └─ cli.py (CLI: mode dispatch, REPL, headless output, tool-confirmation pump)
       ├─ llms/client.py (LLMClient: provider call + tool loop + streaming)
       │    └─ llms/provider.py (ProviderFactory -> Provider)
       │         └─ llms/providers/<name>_provider.py
       ├─ tools/__init__.py (tool schemas, execute_tool_call, output panels)
       │    ├─ tools/function.py (built-in functions from ~/.config/yaicli/functions/)
       │    └─ tools/mcp.py (MCP tools, lazy fastmcp import)
       ├─ chat.py (Chat model + FileChatManager persistence)
       └─ printer.py / render.py (streaming, reasoning, markdown, prompts)

_faststart.main answers -v/--version without importing the config/role/CLI stack (zero filesystem writes) and otherwise delegates to entry.py. entry.py parses arguments (including the headless flags), merges piped stdin, processes --image, then builds a CLI, calls cli.configure_headless(...) and cli.run(...). CLI decides between the single-shot path (_run_once) and the REPL (_run_repl); both assemble messages and ask LLMClient.completion_with_tools() for a response stream. Tool calls come back through the same generator and are executed after the confirmation gate, then the loop calls the provider again with the tool results.

docs.title: Module map
docs.text: Module Responsibility _faststart.py Console entry (ai, yaicli, python -m yaicli); static --version fast path, SIGPIPE/EPIPE handling; then delegates to entry.py. entry.py Typer app/options, stdin/image handling, headless flags, top-level error → exit-code mapping. cli.py CLI orchestrator: temp/chat/exec modes, REPL, chat save/load, role wiring, machine output (json/stream-json), exit-code state contract. errors.py ErrorKind/AgentError, exception classification, retry helpers, EXIT_* constants. cmd_handler.py Slash commands (/add, /context, /save, /mode, ...) and !shell. config.py Layered cfg singleton: env > config.ini > defaults; type conversion. const.py Defaults (DEFAULT_CONFIG_MAP), paths, commands/modes, default roles. console.py YaiConsole singleton, stderr console for machine mode, EPIPE-safe broken-pipe handling, untrusted-text helpers. context.py /add persistent context and @path temporary references (dirs, binaries, images). chat.py Chat message model, JSON serialization, atomic saves, FileChatManager. history.py Bounded prompt-toolkit history file ($XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history or ~/.yaicli_history). role.py Role/RoleManager, role JSON files under ~/.config/yaicli/roles/. schemas.py Shared dataclasses crossing layers: ChatMessage, LLMResponse, ToolCall, ToolPolicy. printer.py / render.py Streaming output, reasoning, confirmation prompts, markdown rendering. image.py --image validation, MIME detection, base64/URL handling. function_schema.py OpenAISchema: pydantic model → OpenAI/Anthropic tool schemas. functions/ Built-in function templates (buildin/) and install/reinstall/list callbacks. llms/ LLMClient, provider ABC/registry, one module per provider. tools/ Tool schema aggregation/caching, function loading, MCP integration, approval store, risk.py (tool risk classes + shell danger classification). utils.py Shell/OS detection, str2bool, option callbacks, event-loop helper.

docs.title: State on disk
docs.text:
The config directory is resolved at import time: YAI_CONFIG_DIR > XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yaicli > %APPDATA%/yaicli (Windows) > ~/.config/yaicli.

  • <config-dir>/config.ini — configuration, created lazily on the first run that needs it and written with mode 0600 (ai --template prints the defaults).
  • <config-dir>/roles/, functions/, mcp.json, tool_permissions.json — user data. functions_manifest.json records the version/hashes used to warn about stale exported copies.
  • tool_audit.jsonl, tool-outputs/ — tool audit log and spilled (untruncated) tool outputs (v0.19; see docs/usage/context-limits.md and docs/usage/permissions.md).
  • $XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history or ~/.yaicli_history — prompt history (bounded by MAX_HISTORY).
  • CHAT_HISTORY_DIR (temp directory by default) — saved chat JSON sessions.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text: TEMP_MODE (single-shot), CHAT_MODE (REPL) and EXEC_MODE (generate + confirm a shell command) are the only runtime modes. --code is not a runtime mode: it selects the Code Assistant role and a plain-text printer. --shell always uses the Shell Command Generator role.

docs.title: Tool-calling loop
docs.text:
1. A per-request ToolPolicy decides whether functions/MCP tools are advertised.
  2. Provider responses carry zero or more complete ToolCalls (streaming providers aggregate per tool index).
  3. LLMClient evaluates the policy, runs each call through the confirmation gate (TOOL_CONFIRM) and execute_tool_call().
  4. Tool results are appended as messages and the provider is called again, up to MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH rounds.

docs.title: CLI Debugging
docs.text: Practical recipes for debugging YAICLI when working from a source checkout.

docs.title: Run the code you are editing
docs.text:
The package does not need to be installed. From the repository root:

# point imports at this checkout and keep user state out of your real HOME
PYTHONPATH=. HOME=/tmp/yaicli-dev COLUMNS=120 python -m yaicli.entry "hello"

python -m yaicli.entry is the same Typer app as the ai console script. A throwaway HOME gives you a fresh config file, roles/functions directories and chat storage, so experiments cannot corrupt your real ~/.config/yaicli.

docs.title: Verbose mode
docs.text:
ai --verbose "hello"

--verbose prints the loaded configuration (API key masked), the current role, provider messages/tools for each request, and tracebacks for handled errors. Do not paste verbose output into bug reports without checking it: only API_KEY is masked, other credentials in EXTRA_HEADERS/provider-specific keys are not.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix Unknown provider: <name> The PROVIDER value is not a ProviderFactory.providers_map key. Run ai --list-providers. API_KEY is required No key in API_KEY, YAI_API_KEY, or the provider-specific fallback. ModelAPIError / HTTP 4xx Check model name, base URL, and provider credentials with --verbose. Config traceback / non-zero exit Malformed config.ini (missing [core], duplicate section). Inspect ai --template for the expected format. Functions behave like an old version Built-in definitions load from the package; stale exported copies live in ~/.config/yaicli/functions/. Run ai --list-functions (reports source + stale copies), then ai --reinstall-functions. Markup/render crash Untrusted strings must go through yaicli/console.py helpers (safe_text, untrusted_text, print_untrusted). Process exits 0 after an error message Should not happen — handled failures exit 1 (entry.py); file a bug with the command and exit code.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: 0 on success, 1 on handled failures (config/provider/API/no-input/depth), 2 on usage errors, 3 when a denied tool is fatal (--fail-on-tool-denied), 130 on SIGINT, 141/0 on a broken pipe. In --chat mode an error in one turn keeps the REPL alive; the exit code reflects leaving the REPL. See Exit codes and Headless & Scripting.

docs.title: Isolate components
docs.text:
• Config: import yaicli.config.cfg and print it; the singleton is built at import time.
  • Provider only: instantiate the provider with a dict config and a mocked CLIENT_CLS, then call _handle_normal_response() / _handle_stream_response() with constructed ChatCompletion / ChatCompletionChunk objects (see tests/llms/).
  • Tool only: call execute_tool_call(ToolCall(...)) with yaicli.tools.cfg patched and get_function/get_mcp mocked (tests/tools/).
  • CLI/REPL: inject a mock client via CLI(client=...); tests/conftest.py provides patched_config_path, setup_test_environment, cli, mock_console.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest tests/test_entry.py tests/test_cli.py -q   # CLI behaviour
uv run pytest -k "markup or confirmation" -q            # safety paths

Use pytest -x --pdb to drop into the debugger on the first failure, and ruff check yaicli tests before pushing.

docs.title: Where to put temporary output
docs.text: Use the project console (get_console()) or print() in entry.py only; remove debug output before committing. tests/ never call real APIs — keep it that way when adding diagnostics.

docs.title: Interleaved Thinking
docs.text: MiniMax-M2.1 and newer models support Interleaved Thinking (交错思维链), which allows the model to reason before each tool use and make decisions based on tool results.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When reasoning_split=True is enabled (default), the API returns reasoning content separately from the main response:

{
    "message": {
        "content": "The weather in Beijing is sunny...",
        "role": "assistant",
        "reasoning_details": [
            {
                "type": "reasoning.text",
                "text": "I need to check the weather for Beijing..."
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Interleaved Thinking is enabled by default for MiniMax provider. You can control it via:

Environment Variable: 

export YAI_MINIMAX_REASONING_SPLIT=true

Config File: 

[core]
MINIMAX_REASONING_SPLIT=true

EXTRA_BODY (advanced): 

EXTRA_BODY={"reasoning_split": true}

Note: When reasoning_split is explicitly set in EXTRA_BODY, it takes precedence over MINIMAX_REASONING_SPLIT.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Reasoning content is preserved in conversation history and sent back to the model in subsequent requests
  • This ensures the model maintains continuity in its thinking process across multiple tool calls
  • Reasoning content is displayed alongside the main response when SHOW_REASONING=true

docs.title: Important Notes

docs.title: Function Calling
docs.text: YAICLI supports function calling: the model can ask YAICLI to execute a local function/tool (for example fs_read_file, web_search, or execute_shell_command) and then continue the conversation with the result.

docs.title: Built-in tools load out of the box
docs.text:
Since v0.19 the 12 built-in tool definitions are loaded directly from the installed package, so the model can call them on the first run with no setup step. ai --install-functions is no longer required (it remains available as an export command, see below).

Loading precedence:

  1. the built-in definitions shipped in the package;
  2. then Python files in the functions directory (<config-dir>/functions/, normally ~/.config/yaicli/functions/); a user file whose tool name matches a built-in overrides it.
  3. A broken function file only disables that file: a warning is printed to stderr and the other tools keep working.
Action Command Effect List tools ai --list-functions Prints every loaded tool with its source (builtin/user) and warns about stale copies. Export editable copies ai --install-functions Copies every built-in definition into the functions directory. Existing files are skipped, so your customisations are never overwritten. Refresh exported copies ai --reinstall-functions Overwrites files matching current built-ins with the new version; custom files (different names) are preserved.

When do I need ai --reinstall-functions? Only when you have exported copies in the functions directory and want the definitions from the new version. If you never ran --install-functions, an upgrade needs no extra step. A stale exported copy is reported once by --list-functions, and the built-in stays active for tool names you did not customise.

Paths on Windows: %APPDATA%\yaicli\functions when APPDATA is set, otherwise C:\Users\<user>\.config\yaicli\functions (the non-Windows path is ~/.config/yaicli/functions/).

docs.title: Writing custom functions
docs.text:
Add a Python file to ~/.config/yaicli/functions/ (files starting with _ are ignored). It must define a class named Function that subclasses yaicli.function_schema.OpenAISchema and a classmethod execute. The tool name is the pydantic model title (class Config: title). Pydantic fields become the tool parameters; use Field(description=...) (and a class docstring) so the model knows how to call it. Example:

from pydantic import Field

from yaicli.function_schema import OpenAISchema


class Function(OpenAISchema):
    """Add two integers and return the result."""

    a: int = Field(..., description="First integer")
    b: int = Field(..., description="Second integer")

    class Config:
        title = "add_numbers"

    @classmethod
    def execute(cls, a: int, b: int) -> str:
        return str(a + b)

Restart ai after adding or changing a custom function; the loader executes every *.py file in that directory at startup. ai --reinstall-functions never deletes custom files, and ai --install-functions only adds built-in files that are missing.

docs.title: Enabling and controlling function calls
docs.text:
• Function calling is enabled by default (ENABLE_FUNCTIONS=true). Toggle it per run with --enable-functions / --disable-functions, or set ENABLE_FUNCTIONS=false in the config file.
  • Function output is displayed by default; use --hide-function-output or set SHOW_FUNCTION_OUTPUT=false to hide it. Long output is truncated in the terminal exactly as it is in the model context (see Context & Limits).
  • Every call asks for confirmation by default (TOOL_CONFIRM=true); see Permissions & Safety for the prompt, risk levels, rules and audit log.
  • MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH (default 8) bounds recursive tool-call rounds in one request; override per run with --max-turns N.

docs.title: Reading Multiple Files in One Call
docs.text:
The built-in fs_read_file function accepts a list of file paths, so several files can be read with a single tool call instead of one call per file:

{"file_paths": ["src/main.py", "src/config.py"], "encoding": "utf-8"}

A single path string is still accepted for backward compatibility. If you keep exported copies of the built-in definitions, refresh them with ai --reinstall-functions after upgrading.

docs.title: Reading Multiple Images in One Call
docs.text:
The built-in fs_read_image function follows the same list-based contract, so several images can be read and base64-encoded in one tool call:

{"image_paths": ["artwork/before.png", "artwork/after.png"]}

A single path string is still accepted for backward compatibility. The same ai --reinstall-functions rule applies to exported copies.

docs.title: Built-in Function Safety
docs.text:
The built-in functions run with your local permissions, so the shipped implementations apply their own guard rails. These are user-visible contracts — if you see different behaviour, run ai --reinstall-functions after upgrading.

fetch_webpage only fetches public http/https URLs:

  • loopback, private, link-local, cloud-metadata (169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200), CGNAT/shared-address (100.64.0.0/10), multicast, reserved, and unspecified addresses are refused before any request is made (IPv4 and IPv6);
  • redirects are followed manually and re-validated hop by hop (maximum 5 redirects); a cross-host redirect does not forward your cookies or Referer, and an https → http downgrade is refused;
  • the response body is capped at 10 MB; timeout, user_agent, cookies, referer, and language are honoured;
  • TLS certificate verification is enabled by default and is never silently disabled on a connection error. Passing verify_ssl=False explicitly is allowed (with a warning) but is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks;
  • every failure is returned to the model as a Failed to fetch ... string instead of raising, so the model can adapt.

fs_edit_file is all-or-nothing:

  • supported operations and keys:
  • replace: {"type": "replace", "old": <str>, "new": <str>} — replaces all occurrences. old must be non-empty and must differ from new;
  • replace_line: {"type": "replace_line", "line_number": <1-based int>, "new": <str>};
  • insert_line: {"type": "insert_line", "line_number": <0..N>, "content": <str>};
  • delete_line: {"type": "delete_line", "line_number": <1-based int>};
  • append: {"type": "append", "content": <str>};
  • every edit is validated and applied in order; if any edit fails, nothing is written and the result reports the failures (success=false, error explains how many failed);
  • writes are atomic and preserve file permissions; a read-only file is rejected with Permission denied instead of being overwritten.

docs.title: Tool Execution Confirmation
docs.text:
By default YAICLI asks for confirmation before running each tool call:

╭─ Confirm tool call ─────────────────────────────────────╮
│ execute_shell_command({"shell_command": "du -sh ."})    │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
Execute tool? [y]once, [a]session, [A]always, [n]o:
Key Meaning y Allow this call only a Allow for the rest of this session A Always allow — saved to tool_permissions.json n Deny — the model receives a refusal result and can adapt

Pressing Ctrl-C or sending EOF at the prompt is treated as a denial.

In non-interactive sessions (piped stdin / no TTY), unapproved tools are denied; pre-approve them with --allowed-tools, --yes (read-level tools only), or persistent rules in tool_permissions.json. Dangerous shell commands always need an explicit confirmation and are refused non-interactively.

This section is only a summary. The full model — risk classes, persistent rules (argv_prefix / path_glob), audit log, and headless approval flags — is documented in Permissions & Safety; the TOOL_CONFIRM=false escape hatch is described there as well.

docs.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
docs.text:
MCP allows AI models to use external tools:

# Enable MCP in queries
ai 'What is the latest exchange rate between BTC and USD?' --enable-mcp

Configure MCP tools in ~/.config/yaicli/mcp.json.

docs.title: Image Input (Vision)
docs.text: YAICLI supports sending images to vision-capable models (GPT-5.2, Claude 3, Gemini, Llama 3.2 Vision, etc.) using the --image / -i option.

docs.title: Local Images
docs.text:
Pass a local image file path. The image will be validated and base64-encoded before sending:

ai --image photo.jpg "What is in this image?"
ai -i screenshot.png "Describe the UI layout"

Supported formats: JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg), PNG (.png), GIF (.gif), WebP (.webp).

docs.title: URL Images
docs.text:
Pass an image URL to send it directly to the provider:

ai --image https://example.com/diagram.png "Explain this architecture"

docs.title: Multiple Images
docs.text:
Use -i multiple times to send multiple images in one request:

ai -i before.png -i after.png "What changed between these two screenshots?"

docs.title: Image-Only Invocation
docs.text:
You can send an image without a text prompt:

ai --image photo.jpg

When no text prompt is given, YAICLI sends a minimal prompt (Describe the image., or Describe these images. for multiple images) so providers always receive a valid user message.

docs.title: Provider Compatibility
docs.text:
Image input is automatically formatted for each provider family:

Provider Family Providers Image Format OpenAI-compatible OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, etc. (~25) content array with image_url blocks Anthropic Anthropic, Anthropic Bedrock, Anthropic Vertex content array with image + source blocks Gemini Gemini, Vertex AI Part.from_bytes() / Part.from_uri() Ollama Ollama Separate images array (base64 only)

Providers without vision support (Cohere, HuggingFace, ChatGLM, ModelScope) will show a warning and send text-only messages.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Image input is supported in single-shot mode only, not in interactive --chat mode
  • No client-side file size limit; the provider API enforces its own limits
  • Ollama may not support URL images; use local files instead
  • No automatic image resizing or optimization

docs.title: LLM Provider Configuration
docs.text:
YAICLI works with many LLM providers. Configure your preferred provider in the config file:

[core]
# Comments must be on their own line; inline comments become part of the value.
PROVIDER=openai
# Leave BASE_URL empty to use the provider default URL.
BASE_URL=
API_KEY=your_api_key_here
MODEL=gpt-5.2

docs.title: Syntax Highlighting Themes
docs.text:
Change the code highlighting theme:

CODE_THEME = monokai

Browse available themes at: https://pygments.org/styles/

docs.title: Extra Headers and Body Parameters
docs.text:
Add custom parameters to API requests:

EXTRA_HEADERS={"X-Extra-Header": "value"}
EXTRA_BODY={"extra_key": "extra_value"}

Example for Qwen3's thinking behavior:

EXTRA_BODY={"enable_thinking": false}
# Or limit thinking tokens:
EXTRA_BODY={"thinking_budget": 4096}

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: YAICLI offers multiple ways to interact with AI models directly from your command line.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Give the agent a multi-step task (it picks and runs tools itself):

ai "Use your tools to find the 3 largest files here and write a summary to REPORT.md"

Get a quick answer.

ai "What is the capital of France?"

Start an interactive chat session 

ai --chat

Generate and execute shell commands 

ai --shell "Create a backup of my Documents folder"

Generate code snippets, default in Python 

ai --code "Write a Python function to sort a list"

Read stdin from pipe 

cat app.py | ai "Explain what this code does"

Debug with verbose mode 

ai --verbose "Explain quantum computing"

This help snapshot is abbreviated; run ai --help for the authoritative current options (see also Command Reference and Headless & Scripting).

docs.title: Image Input
docs.text:
Send images to vision-capable models directly from the command line using --image / -i:

# Describe a local image
ai --image photo.jpg "What is in this image?"

# Compare multiple images
ai -i img1.png -i img2.png "What are the differences?"

# Use an image URL
ai --image https://example.com/diagram.png "Explain this diagram"

# Send image without text prompt
ai --image photo.jpg

When you omit the prompt, YAICLI sends a minimal prompt (Describe the image., or Describe these images. for several images) together with the image.

Supported formats: JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg), PNG (.png), GIF (.gif), WebP (.webp).

Note: Image input works in single-shot mode only (not --chat). Providers without vision support will show a warning and ignore the images.
